fragments.text: Let's ask Zai for the cross tab

reply_text:
㊥ (cross-tab to Zai) zai-1 is running the cross-tab now. It compares the loop stage from each turn's retrieved pattern with the stage of the 象 intent read from your wording. Where the two agree, it checks whether the intent's R-node picks out one node within the stage. I'll report back when it's done.

㊢ (what I asked for) The inputs are the existing records, which Zai will only read:
- the pattern joins and stage labels for 22 August to 1 October;
- the turn analyses in `~/.emacs-graph/session-turn-analysis` (1,176 have an agent interpretation);
- the intent table in `core.cljs`, parsed from the file, not copied by hand.

Zai has to name the key it uses to match a turn to its pattern row, and count the turns that match and those that don't. The output covers:
- a stage-by-stage agreement matrix;
- for turns where the stages agree, which R-nodes the intents fall on;
- how often an intent's R-node equals the R-node the pattern was already labelled with, for the 66 patterns that have one;
- example turns where the stages disagree most.

Zai also writes a small test on a hand-worked fixture. Everything lands in `futon0/analysis/audits`.

㊢ (tracking) Zai job `invoke-1790893424519-29906-ca88b424`, park `park-aeb711c6-…`, 45-minute deadline. Kimi's one-page Minard job (`…dcce93af`) is still running with its own park. When each reports back, I'll check its work and bring you the result.

㊥ (cross-tab result) The cross-tab says no: within the five loop stages, a turn's pattern stage and its intent stage agree no more often than chance (κ about 0). So intent can't choose the R-node within a pattern's stage. Zai's summary says the intent R-nodes "spread across the stage", but that only repeats which intents are common overall. Of the two options from before, that leaves the direct patterns-to-R-numbers labelling.

㊬ (what I checked) futon0 `4f8f8244`, by zai-1:
- **Files:** the commit has only the four files I asked for. The intent table is parsed from `core.cljs`, not retyped.
- **Join:** it is exact. The pattern row's `turn-id` equals the turn record's `evidence_id`. I matched three turns by hand, and the text, timestamp and pattern line up in each.
- **Coverage:** only 331 of the 4,059 pattern-labelled turns have a 象 reading with an evidence id, nearly all from the last week or so.
- **Tests:** they pass when run as `python3 -m unittest crosstab_stage_intent`. The separate test file is a wrapper that plain `unittest` doesn't pick up, which is untidy.
- **Fixture:** the hand-worked fixture test exercises the matrix and agreement functions, not the join itself.

㊩ (why the headline numbers need a chance baseline) Zai reports 12.7% agreement, and it compares that to the earlier PBASE check (κ 0.010). But that figure includes assurance, coordination and none turns, which no intent maps to, so they count as automatic disagreements. I recomputed on the five loop stages only, with an expected-by-chance baseline:

| Unit | Turns or pairs | Agreement | Expected by chance | κ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Each (turn, intent) pair | 626 pairs | 18.8% | 20.1% | −0.015 |
| First intent per turn | 187 turns | 26.2% | 21.3% | 0.06 |

For the R-nodes inside "agreeing" pairs, such as BELIEVE R3 25, R7 10 or SELECT R6 29: when the stages only agree at chance, that spread follows from how common each intent is overall. It doesn't show the intent picking out a node.

🈖 (what this suggests) The two labels seem to describe different things about the same turn. The pattern says what the turn is working on, as retrieved from the library. The intent says what kind of conversational move you made, such as reporting, asking or delegating. A "report" lands on PERCEIVE/R2 whatever its subject is. So the intent table describes your move in the conversation, not the War Machine step the turn's subject belongs to. That's worth knowing for the AIF model, since the two could become separate observation channels instead of one being used to refine the other.

㊭ (next step for R-numbers) For the patterns-to-R-numbers alignment:
1. Label the functional (practice) patterns only, by reading their THEN clause.
2. Choose only among the R-nodes in the pattern's own stage, with "none" allowed.
3. Go by hits: the top ~150 patterns cover most of the traffic. The 66 existing labels are mostly patterns *about* a component, so they'd be kept separately as topic labels.
4. Check the result against what the agent did next, which is the test the intent table's own notes propose.

Per the batching rule, that's about 15 jobs of 10 patterns each for Kimi or Zai, with a checker after each chunk.

🈸 (go-ahead) Shall I start that labelling, beginning with SELECT and BELIEVE, where the ambiguity is largest?

Now planting a bug in a copy — believe drops one family band — to see the check catch it:Caught on both click and keyboard. Looking at the screenshots:Looks right. Publishing, then running the check against the published copy:㊥ (one interactive infographic) The merged figure is live at https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/wip/audits/minard-operator-work-2026-10-01.html. Click a stage band or its legend button, or tab to it and press Enter, and that stage opens into its pattern families just below the main figure. The family panel uses the same time axis and the same thickness scale, and has the 21 September marker. The other stages fade while one is open. "← All stages" or Escape closes it, and hovering over a family gives its exact hits for that day.

㊬ (what I checked) futon0 `f1d2b23`, by kimi-1:
- **Files:** the commit has the new build script, the template, the rebuilt page and the Playwright check. It also includes my earlier `tokenDataEnd` fix to the 10-01 template, which I hadn't committed. The 09-21 page rebuilds byte-identical, and the families numbers come from the existing builder.
- **Planted bug:** I made a copy that drops one believe family band. The check failed on it for both the click and the Enter key ("drawn=8 expected=9").
- **Playwright run:** I ran it myself on the real page and on the published copy fetched back from the site (identical bytes); all checks passed both times.
- **Screenshots:** I looked at assurance opened and believe opened. Both look as described, with the hover readout working.

㊟ (limits of the check) The check compares the bands drawn against the data embedded in the page. Whether that data is right is covered by the separate Python test that sums families to the stage totals. Also, the family panel's date ticks fall on different days from the main figure's (29 Aug, 05 Sep vs 22 Aug, 26 Aug). The time axis is the same, but the gridlines don't line up by eye. I can tidy that if it bothers you.

🈸 (R-number labelling, from the cross-tab) The question from the cross-tab result is still open: shall I start the direct pattern-to-R-node labelling with SELECT and BELIEVE?

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what's in the existing labels) The field is `:node` in `futon0/analysis/audits/pattern-stages-2026-10-01.edn`, filled during the same hand coding that set the stages.
- **TRACE:** has the most, 25 patterns and 99 hits, nearly all assurance practices such as changelog-trail and term-to-channel-traceability.
- **Loop R-nodes:** most have one to five patterns, and most of those are the `problems/rN-…` and `aif/…` entries describing the component itself. Examples are `problems/r10-scheduled-entrypoint` and `aif/interoceptive-tripwires`.
- **Topical vs functional:** 38 of the 66 are topical subject patterns, against 27 that are functional practices.
- **Coverage:** R12, R13 and R11 have one hit each. R19, R3a, CTAU and GRAIN-GATE have none.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(where the one-to-many lives) The stages split as follows in `p4ng/empirics-futon/control-stages.edn`:
- **PERCEIVE:** R2, R8, R19
- **BELIEVE:** R1, R3, R3a, R7
- **EVALUATE:** R4, R5, plus the two CTAU nodes
- **SELECT:** R6, R13, R14, R15, R11, plus GRAIN-GATE
- **ACT:** R16 only

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(a second signal we already have) The intent table in `futon3/src-cljs/futon3/turnfeed/core.cljs` assigns each 象 intent an R-node. That assignment is claude-12's untested proposal from 25 September. It is independent of the patterns: patterns come from what a turn retrieves, intents from how the annotator reads your wording. Where a turn has both and they agree on the stage, the intent could pick the R-node within the stage. One example would be a SELECT pattern plus a "prioritize" intent. I'd start with a cross-tabulation, before relabelling any patterns:
1. Take turns with a stage from their pattern and an intent from 象.
2. Count how often the two agree on the stage.
3. Within agreeing turns, see how evenly the intent's R-nodes spread.
